text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi met the medallists of the Commonwealth Games 2026 at his residence in New Delhi yesterday. During the interaction, the medal winners shared their experiences from the Games with the Prime Minister. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that each one of them has made the nation proud through their exceptional performances and their success will motivate many youngsters. Mr Modi shared a video message and said that those who will play will flourish and appealed to the citizens to always cheer for Bharat.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhli Khadse were present on the occasion. India finished at the 4th spot on the medal table during the games held between 23rd July and the 2nd of this month at Glasgow in Scotland. Indian athletes won 39 medals, including 13 Gold, 17 silver and nine bronze across various sports.

. Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that the Government is cognizant of the risks associated with children’s online activities, including exposure to harmful content, cyberbullying, online exploitation and digital addiction.In a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said that the Government keeps itself informed of global developments and evolving international regulatory approaches relating to online safety, including measures adopted by different jurisdictions for protection of children in the digital environment. He said that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) has been enacted, which establishes the legal framework to regulate the processing of digital personal data.The DPDP Act provides a legal framework for safeguarding children’s privacy online. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Ministry is implementing a project on Information Security Education and Awareness for generating human resources in Information Security and creating general awareness on various aspects of cyber hygiene & cyber security among the masses.

. Sagnik Roy and Sayantan Kushari won the gold medal in the Under-31 Pairs at the 9th World Youth Transnational Championships in Hefei, China, yesterday. In the first elimination round, 34 pairs competed and the top 14 advanced to Flight A, including the Indian duo. They then competed in a round-robin format, with Sagnik and Sayantan finishing on top with 377.67 match points. M Fereneca and F Katusich of Croatia finished second with 357.78 match points, while China’s J Han and Z Wang took the third spot with 335.92 match points.

. Russia has proposed exploring a railway route to the Indian Ocean and India to reduce dependence on strategically important maritime routes. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin said alternative routes could help address risks associated with the two strategic waterways including the Strait of Hormuz and the Bosphorus Strait.According to Russia’s state news agency, Mr. Khusnullin said rail routes passing through Turkmenistan, Iran and Afghanistan could be explored to provide access to India. The proposal comes amid the ongoing conflict in West Asia, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.The proposed railway could have wider geopolitical and economic implications, as it may provide Russia with an alternative overland link towards the Indian Ocean through Central and South Asia.

. Ukraine has reached an agreement with the United States on monthly deliveries of interceptor missiles for the Patriot air defence system. Speaking to reporters in Belgrade, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Washington will supply Ukraine with interceptor missiles on a monthly basis. However, he stressed that the volume falls short of meeting the country’s air defence needs.Zelensky noted that the number of interceptor missiles Ukraine is expected to receive in 2026 would be lower than in 2025, without disclosing specific figures. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy made a landmark first visit to Serbia yesterday to expand cooperation with the Balkan country whose leader has been scaling back once-close ties with Russia.Zelenskyy and his Serbian counterpart Aleksandar Vucic told reporters in Belgrade after their meeting that both countries will work together on the common goal of joining the European Union and intend to finalize a mutual free trade agreement by the end of the year. Vucic’s government also pledged more humanitarian aid, infrastructure and energy equipment for Ukraine.

. The two-day BRICS WAVES Bazaar, a premier international marketplace for the creative economy began in Mumbai today. The event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency brings together over 500 delegates from BRICS members and partners from 21 countries with an aim to create stronger pathways for collaboration across film, television, animation, VFX, gaming, music, digital media and emerging content formats.Information and Broadcasting Secretary, Mr. Chanchal Kumar said WAVES Bazaar seeks to become a platform for the global creative economy where projects are discovered, partnerships are initiated, co-productions are discussed and new markets are opened. Delivering the keynote address in the opening ceremony, Maharashtra’s Minister of Electronics, IT, AI and Culture, Adv. Ashish Shelar said the BRICS WAVES Bazaar is a high-level, curated confluence designed to shape the future of the global creative economy. The event features high-level conferences, keynote addresses, panel discussions, business networking sessions, and curated Business-to-Business meetings.

. India’s national public procurement platform, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has achieved a cumulative Gross Merchandise Value of over 20 lakh crore rupees in the last ten years. GeM was launched on 9th August 2016 to transform public procurement through technology, transparency, efficiency and good governance. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, GeM CEO Mihir Kumar said that the GeMs  business has grown from 422 crore rupees in 2016-17 to over 20 lakh crore rupees now. He said that over the past decade, GeM has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s digital governance ecosystem.Mr Kumar informed that according to a study done by IIT Delhi, the items sold on GeM was cheaper on 74 per cent items in comparison with other e marketplace like Amazon, Flipkart and India Mart. He said, the sellers on GeM platform have grown from around three thousand to over 25 lakh, while the Micro and Small Enterprises registered on the platform have also risen from around two thousand to more than 12 lakh.    Mr Kumar said that today all States are onboarded on GeM platform and soon it will reach out to Urban Local Bodies and Gram Panchayats to expand its business.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. India has crossed 300 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity generation capacity. Akashvani correspondent reports that the milestone of crossing 300 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity generation capacity represents more than 60 per cent of the 500 gigawatts capacity target set for 2030. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy said that the share of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity in the country’s total installed electricity generation capacity has reached over 54 per cent. It added that the growth in clean energy generation has been driven by strong contributions across sectors.In the total Non-Fossil Fuel Capacity of the country, solar energy has remained a key growth engine, with around 165 gigawatts of installed capacity at present. According to the Ministry, a record 55.29 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity was added in the country during 2025-26.The rapid progress in renewable energy capacity is also reflected in renewable energy generation, which has increased from nearly 191 billion units in 2014-15 to over 477 billion units in 2025-26.The Ministry further said that the clean energy transition is no longer just a climate commitment, it is central to shaping India’s industrial competitiveness, energy independence, and economic resilience.

. The government has said that more than one crore 73  lakh e-Passports have been issued so far in India and abroad. In a written reply in Rajya Sabha today, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said that currently, all Regional Passport Offices, Passport Seva Kendras and Post Office Passport Seva Kendras in India and all the Indian Missions abroad are issuing e-Passports. He informed that the e-Passport was launched in May last year. Mr Singh said that the Passport Seva Programme provided comprehensive digital platforms. This includes the Passport Seva Portal, Passport Seva Mobile Apps and a centralised citizen service call centre, enabling applicants to access information, track application status and obtain responses to routine queries without visiting Regional Passport Offices. The Minister said, these digital initiatives have substantially reduced the need for physical visits for administrative enquiries while improving accessibility, convenience and service delivery.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today met the medal winners of the Commonwealth Games 2026 at his residence in New Delhi.Sharing a video message, Mr Modi said that those who participate in sports will prosper and urged citizens to always cheer for Bharat.India finished at the fourth spot on the medal table at the Games, held in Glasgow, Scotland between 23rd of July and 2nd of August. Indian athletes won 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, across various sporting disciplines.

. Iran insists on US Concessions before opening the Strait of Hormuz. Security Chief of Iran, Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, has issued a list of demands for the US to fulfill before Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Published by state media, the list includes measures such as lifting the US naval blockade, withdrawing military forces and permanently ending the war. Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Zolghadr, also called for the US to compensate Iran for damage caused by the conflict and release frozen Iranian assets.

. In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index dropped 0.6 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dipped 0.1 per cent. Major European indices were trading on a positive note today. Germany’s DAX added over 0.8 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 rose more than 0.7 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya has called for greater transparency in athlete selection, athlete-centric governance and institutional reforms in the country’s sports ecosystem. Addressing the National Sports Federation Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today, Dr. Mandaviya said, the interests and welfare of athletes must remain the foremost priority for all stakeholders. He stressed that no athlete should ever face injustice.The Minister called for complete transparency in selection trials, saying open trials should be recorded on camera in the presence of observers to ensure fairness and accountability.On doping, Dr. Mandaviya called for a comprehensive strategy to eliminate the menace from Indian sports. He said, action should not be limited to athletes and that the entire chain, including manufacturers, suppliers, facilitators and users, must be dealt with through a transparent and robust mechanism.The Minister also stressed the need to strengthen India’s indigenous coaching ecosystem and reduce overdependence on foreign coaches. The conclave reviewed the compliance of National Sports Federations with the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, good governance practices and India’s preparedness for the Asian Games 2026, Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and Commonwealth Games 2030.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. The Ministry of Civil Aviation has said that a DGCA Air Safety team will conduct a preliminary investigation into a runway excursion incident involving a Cessna C172-type aircraft at Baramati Airfield in Maharashtra.The Ministry said that the team will ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident. The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies training exercise.During the course of the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of Runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion. The Ministry informed that no injuries or fatalities were reported. It said, the aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. The Ministry said, a detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities.

. Amid ongoing student protests, three serving members of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) have resigned from their posts. JPSC members Ajita Bhattacharya, Jameel Ahmed and Anima Hansda submitted their resignations to Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar yesterday. The resignations of three JPSC members have been accepted by the Governor following a recommendation from the state government.

. India’s capital markets remained resilient during the financial year 2025-26 despite global uncertainties, with India retaining the top position globally in the number of Initial Public Offerings (IPO) and ranking third in funds raised.According to SEBI’s Annual Report released yesterday, the regulator said, the primary equity market remained strong even as corporate bond mobilisation declined by 8.4 per cent to 9.1 lakh crore rupees, marking the first fall in four years. Public debt issuances, however, rose nearly 39 per cent, while municipal bond fundraising surged to one thousand 756 crore rupees through 14 issues.SEBI also introduced a new Closing Auction Session (CAS) to improve price discovery and align India’s markets with global standards. The report noted that foreign portfolio investor (FPI) ownership fell to a 15-year low, while domestic institutional investors (DII) reached a record 17 per cent equity holding by March 2026.Mutual fund participation continued to expand, driven largely by Tier-3 cities, with monthly SIP contributions touching a record average of over 16,400 crore rupees. It also said, 62 per cent of retail investors are influenced by financial influencers on social media, prompting stronger investor protection measures.The regulator outlined several initiatives for the coming year, including Project Jagrook for investor awareness, an AI-enabled WhatsApp campaign, simplified nomination norms, a fast-track mechanism for alternative investment funds, the SEBI Setu portal, and a pilot project for tokenisation of corporate bonds using distributed ledger technology.

. Indian lifters continued their impressive performance at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, today, with a gold and a silver medal in the men’s junior 60-kilogram category. Tomchou Meetei won a total of three medals – gold in the overall category, bronze in the snatch and silver in the clean and jerk.He finished with a combined lift of 266 kilograms. Gurunaidu Sanapathi bagged two medals – silver in the overall category and silver in the snatch, along with bronze in the clean and jerk. He finished with a total lift of 265 kilograms. The two Indian lifters finished just one kilogram apart in the overall standings, giving India a one-two finish in the category.

. India has dispatched an 8 MT consignment of life-saving and essential medicines to Bolivia in support of its public healthcare capacity. The External Affairs Ministry said in a social media post that India always stands ready to advance cooperation through solidarity and shared progress.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers of Indian equities during the first week of August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested Rs 12, 921 crore in the domestic stock market so far this month. The buying momentum, which gathered pace in July, has continued into August, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals and strong quarterly earnings reports.Meanwhile, the debt market has seen a mixed trend in flows. So far in August, Foreign Portfolio Investors have invested 622 crore rupees in debt securities through the General Limit route. However, the Fully Accessible and Voluntary Retention Routes have witnessed outflows of over Rs 350 crore during the period under review.

. The government has extended the tenure of the Director of the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Rahul Navin, by one year from the 13th of this month to the 13th of August next year. The extension in service will continue beyond his scheduled retirement on the 31st of July, 2027. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has given its approval to extend the tenure of Rahul Navin, who is a 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer.

. Indian weightlifter Maharajan Arumugapandian clinched the silver medal in the men’s 65 kg category at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan today.Maharajan produced a new personal best total of 285 kilograms, lifting 128 kg in the snatch and 157 kg in the clean and jerk to secure silver. Vietnam’s Hoang Thach claimed the gold medal with a total lift of 291 kilograms, finishing six kilograms ahead of Maharajan.

. Global crude oil prices dropped today ​as investors weighed signals that Gulf states and Iran were closing in on a deal to reopen the ‌Strait of Hormuz under a temporary arrangement. Brent crude was trading 0.8 per cent down at 81 US dollars and 86 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.3 per cent lower at 77 US dollars and eight cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has proposed a stricter regulatory framework for Authorised Persons (APs) to strengthen investor protection, improve supervision and enhance accountability of stockbrokers. The proposals have been issued through a consultation paper prepared jointly by stock exchanges in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Public comments have been invited till 27th of this month.Under the proposed framework, individual Authorised Persons will be required to maintain a minimum net worth of five lakh rupees, while partnership firms, LLPs and body corporates will need a minimum net worth of 25 lakh rupees.The proposals also mandate disclosure of all banks and demat accounts, business-related websites and social media handles, besides technology-based safeguards such as geo-tagging, CCTV surveillance and biometric authentication at trading terminals. Stockbrokers will be responsible for the acts of their Authorised Persons and will be required to conduct regular inspections, surprise audits and enhanced monitoring to safeguard investors.
. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat gold was trading 0.4 percent up at 1,49,340 rupees per 10 grams, while silver was trading 0.6 percent down at 2,27,030 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.

. Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has unveiled a special Metro train wrapped with the Har Ghar Tiranga theme on the Yellow Line to celebrate the spirit of independence.In a social media post, DMRC said that the train was unveiled as part of the week-long activities being organised to celebrate the 80th Independence Day of India. The Corporation said that the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign this year celebrates the momentous occasion of the 150th year of India’s national song, Vande Mataram. It encouraged citizens to proudly hoist the National Flag and participate in the digital events.

. India’s medal tally rises to three at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in the United States. India’s Basant Kumar Meghwal wins a silver in the high jump, while Shahnavaz Khan wins a bronze in the long jump today. In the men’s high jump, 19-year-old Meghwal cleared his personal best of 2.21 metres to win a silver medal. He became the first Indian to win a medal in the high jump at the World U-20 Championships. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took the bronze.In the men’s long jump, Shahnavaz clinched bronze with a best effort of 7.84 metres. The 18-year-old produced his best jump in his third attempt. Italy’s Daniele Inzoli won the gold medal with a jump of 7.97 metres, while Australia’s Mason McGroder took silver with a personal best of 7.96 metres. Earlier, in the javelin throw, Ashish Yadav won silver and became the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win at the World Athletics U20 Championships. Yadav produced his best throw of 74.09 metres in the third round yesterday.

. The enhanced southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones have affected more than 3.8 lakh people across eight regions in the Philippines. According to the Philippine News Agency, 1.1 lakh families were affected, with six deaths and seven injuries reported.The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council of the Philippines said 86 evacuation centres have been activated, sheltering about 7,300 people. Another 3,700 people are staying outside evacuation centres.The National Weather Service agency PAGASA warned that the southwest monsoon will continue to bring heavy rain to Metro Manila and several provinces in Luzon. It warned of possible flash floods and landslides in Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro. Scattered rain and thunderstorms are also expected in the Visayas and parts of Mindanao. PAGASA said Typhoon Dolphin is strengthening the southwest monsoon, with rough to very rough seas expected off extreme Northern Luzon.

. The ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign has begun across Maharashtra with patriotic fervour. Various districts in the state are organising Tiranga rallies and awareness programmes ahead of Independence Day.In Beed, a Tiranga rally was organised from the District Sports Complex by the district administration, the District Sports Officer’s Office and various sports organisations. A large number of sportspersons, students, sports coaches and citizens participated in the rally. Slogans of ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ and ‘Vande Mataram’ created a patriotic atmosphere in the city.In Thane, a Tiranga cycle rally was organised jointly by the Thane Municipal Corporation and Aamhi Cycle Premi Foundation. The rally, which began from the Municipal Corporation headquarters, witnessed enthusiastic participation by cyclists and citizens. The rally highlighted the messages of patriotism, environmental conservation, healthy living and greater use of bicycles.In Khamgaon in Buldhana district, a Tiranga Yatra and public awareness rally were organised under the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’, ‘TB-Free India’ and ‘Drug-Free India’ campaigns. NCC cadets, students, voluntary organisations and citizens participated in the rally. Students also presented street plays at various locations to create awareness about tuberculosis, its symptoms, prevention and free treatment.The ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign is being observed across the state through various activities aimed at strengthening the spirit of patriotism and encouraging citizens to actively participate in Independence Day celebrations.

. The Government has said that the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs has emerged as a single point of access to consumers across the country for their grievance redressal at a pre-litigation stage. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution B L Verma said that consumers can register their grievances from all over the country in 17 languages through a toll-free number 1915.The Minister also said that 1,853 companies, who have voluntarily partnered with NCH, as part of the ‘Convergence’ programme directly respond to these grievances according to their redressal process and revert by providing a feedback to the complainant on the portal. Mr Verma also informed that NCH has successfully facilitated refunds amounting to over 91 crore rupees (including over 63 Crore rupees with regard to the grievances pertaining to e-commerce sector) to consumers between 25th April 2025 and 30th June 2026 by effectively addressing over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha has reached the women’s singles final of the Korea Masters Super 300 badminton tournament in Asan, South Korea. Ashmita defeated fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal today.The victory comes after Ashmita produced the biggest upset of the tournament in the quarterfinals, defeating top seed and world number 22 Hina Akechi of Japan in a three-game thriller.Ashmita will face China’s Q Han in the women’s singles final tomorrow. Han reached the final after defeating South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, 21-14 in the other semifinal.

. Indian weightlifter Titli Maji clinched a silver medal in the women’s 45kg category, marking an impressive start for the country at the Asian Youth and Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, today.  She secured the medal with a total lift of 145kg, comprising 65kg in the snatch and 80kg in the clean and jerk. Parishmita Gogoi finished fourth in the same event. The competition will continue until August 14.

. The Government today said that it has strengthened the legal and institutional framework to deal with online piracy of cinematograph films, including unauthorized dissemination of films through intermediaries such as Telegram. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L Murugan said, the Cinematograph Act, 1952 was amended through the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 to introduce specific provisions to curb unauthorized recording and exhibition of films. The Minister also said that the newly inserted Section 7(1B)(ii) empowers the Government, under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, to take action against intermediaries hosting pirated content. Mr. Murugan informed that under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, the intermediaries are required to remove any content violative of any law for the time being in force as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a notice by appropriate government or its authorized agency.

. In Japan, Nagasaki today marks the 81st anniversary of the US atomic bombing. On the occasion, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi reiterated her policy of taking a realistic and pragmatic approach toward achieving a world without nuclear weapons.Talking to reporters, she said Japan’s policy is to work within the Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty. On the occasion, representatives from more than 90 countries attended the ceremony at the Peace Park, Nagasaki and observed a moment of silence at 11:02 a.m.On 9th August, 1945 United States had dropped on Nagasaki a plutonium device called “Fat Man,” killing an estimated 74,000 people by the end of the year and leading directly to Japan’s unconditional surrender.

. The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is being celebrated nationwide to foster a sense of patriotism among citizens, strengthen national unity, and promote India’s cultural heritage. The campaign marks the fifth year of the Har Ghar Tiranga initiative, which began in 2022 and has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements.The initiative is aimed at encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag and participate in activities celebrating patriotism, national unity and India’s cultural heritage. This year’s campaign holds special significance as it coincides with the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram,” bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. As part of the celebrations, mass singing of Vande Mataram will be organised across the country.In Delhi, as part of the campaign, Lok Sabha BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj paid floral tribute at the memorial of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in Malviya Nagar followed by a Tiranga Yatra from Pilanji Village to Greater Kailash. Speaking to the media, Ms Swaraj said that this Independence Day is particularly special as India marks its 80th. She added that the BJP has launched a week-long campaign starting today, during which party office-bearers and workers will visit the memorials of national heroes and martyrs.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said, credit extended by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) grew by 14.4 per cent year-on-year in June 2026, compared to 11.1 per cent a year earlier.According to the RBI, credit to agriculture and allied activities rose 17.9 per cent, up from 5.1 per cent a year ago. Retail loan growth accelerated to 20.3 per cent from 14.3 per cent, driven by strong growth in housing, vehicle loans and loans against gold jewellery. However, credit growth to the services sector moderated to 17.6 per cent from 22.4 percent, while lending to industry slowed to 6.7 percent from 10.3 percent, mainly due to subdued growth in infrastructure lending.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in negative territory today. The Sensex fell 456 points or 0.6 per cent to close at 78,499. The Nifty dropped 65 points or 0.3 per cent to settle at 24,571.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index rose 0.2 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index ended marginally down.Earlier, the markets opened with a gap-down as crude oil prices rose amid renewed concerns over the Strait of Hormuz. The Sensex and the Nifty traded with losses throughout  the session.In the Sensex pack, 16 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top laggards, Bajaj Finance lost six per cent, Bajaj Finserv shed 4.2 per cent and ICICI Bank dropped  3.7 per cent. In contrast, Tata Consultancy Services climbed 3.5 per cent,  Mahindra and Mahindra increased 2.5 per cent and State Bank of India rose over one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 17 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, Focused IT advanced over 1.4 per cent, Auto rose 1.3 per cent and Hospitals gained over 1.2 per cent. In contrast, Financial Services dipped over 1.3 per cent, Private Banks as well as Top 10 Banks shed nearly one per cent and Consumer Durables lost 0.9 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,209 companies declined, 2,044 advanced and 207 remained unchanged.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 10.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 692.8 billion US dollars during the week ended July 31. According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 8.7 billion USD to 564.6 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves added 1.6 billion USD to 104.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights increased by 48 million USD to 18.66 billion USD. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by 28 million USD to around 4.8 billion USD.

. The United States has rejected China’s move to establish what it called a national nature reserve at Scarborough Reef, saying the measure could restrict Filipino fishermen’s access to their traditional fishing grounds, as reflected in the 2016 Arbitral Award. In a press release, the US State Department said this is yet another unilateral attempt by China to use dubious environmental and legal pretexts, backed by coercion, to advance its sweeping territorial and maritime claims in the South China Sea at the expense of its neighbours.The United States stands with its Ally, the Philippines, in support of a free and open Indo-Pacific, the statement further said. The statement followed China’s announcement of new management measures for the disputed feature, referred to by the Philippines and international legal documents as Scarborough Shoal. According to China Daily, the measures were issued on August 1 and consist of 16 articles aimed at managing the newly established national nature reserve. The measures establish a coordination mechanism among the four agencies to address major issues, strengthen cooperation and information-sharing, and enhance supervision and law enforcement against activities deemed illegal.The 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award, issued by the arbitral tribunal constituted under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), found that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources within the maritime areas falling within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone. However, China has rejected the same.

. The Pentagon has ordered US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries as the Iran war has depleted key US munitions stockpiles. The Washington Post reported that Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg told defense industry leaders in a memo that they have 21 days to submit plans to drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and increased production for critical capabilities.The Pentagon has also pursued framework agreements with major defense contractors and technology firms to expand production. But those agreements are nonbinding and depend on congressional funding. The directive comes as the Pentagon seeks to replenish stocks of weapons, including Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors.The Center for Strategic and International Studies said the global inventory of Patriot missiles had fallen from about 2,200 before the war to fewer than 827, while THAAD stocks dropped from 452 to less than 278. The Pentagon’s push comes as a 1.15 trillion US Dollar defense spending bill remains stalled in Congress, potentially delaying efforts to rapidly expand weapons production.

The Government today said India has been advocating for early commencement of text-based negotiations with clearly laid out timelines and milestones regarding permanent membership for India in an expanded United Nations Security Council (UNSC). In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh today said that India consistently highlights the need for expanding both permanent and non-permanent categories in UNSC and greater representation of the developing countries, with emphasis on the Global South.The External Affairs Ministry has taken up the matter of permanent membership for India both bilaterally and multilaterally at various levels, including at the highest levels. The MoS said that Ministry’s engagements in this regard cover various countries, including all five permanent members of the UNSC. Mr Singh said that the government strongly believes that India has all the credentials to be a permanent member of a reformed and expanded UNSC that reflects contemporary global realities.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha produced a superb comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026, beating China’s Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final this morning. The Assam shuttler recovered from losing the opening game to prevail 14-21, 21-14, and 21-14 in 53 minutes and claim her first BWF title. Earlier, Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, and 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final. Ashmita Chaliha had won the gold medal at the 2024 Asia Team Championships. At the 2019 South Asian Games, she had secured gold medals in both the women’s singles and team events.

In a significant initiative to encourage and promote emerging filmmaking talent from the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) has announced the IFFJK Emerging Filmmakers Competition 2026, as part of the scheduled 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK). Registrations for the competition has commenced from today. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the competition is exclusively open to aspiring filmmakers from J&K and aims to provide a prestigious platform for young storytellers to showcase their creativity, cinematic vision and technical skills through original short films.The aspiring and emerging filmmakers are invited to submit original short films with a maximum duration of five minutes and the last date for submission is August 26. The applicants must be between 18 and 39 years of age as on September 1, 2026, and possess a valid domicile certificate of J&K. The competition is being organised around the theme “Rang-e-Cinema: Frames of a New Jammu & Kashmir”, reflecting the evolving cultural, social and creative narratives of the region while encouraging youth to present compelling stories through the medium of cinema. Interested filmmakers and cinematographers are advised to register by visiting the official IFFJK website www.iffjk.org and the detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and the registration process are also available on this website for ease of aspirants. DIPR urges aspiring filmmakers from across J&K to seize this opportunity and contribute towards strengthening the Union Territory’s growing film culture through innovative and impactful storytelling.

. Indian grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa has clinched the Grand Chess Tour St. Louis Rapid and Blitz title in the United States. The 20-year-old secured the championship after drawing against Uzbekistan’s Grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the penultimate round, finishing the tournament with 23 points out of a possible 35.Praggnanandhaa maintained the lead throughout the five-day event, with  Sindarov mounted a strong challenge in the final stages but fell short, finishing runner-up with a 1.5-point deficit.Earlier in June, Praggnanandhaa scripted history by claiming the Norway Chess 2026 crown in Oslo after defeating Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the tenth and final round.
